classification.difficultyReason: Use the stated rectangular block dimensions to select a volume subtraction, identify the removed hemisphere as half a sphere and invert the explicitly taught volume formula with an exact cube root. The single target and shape are supplied; several linked routine decisions, without an unsignposted proof or novel construction.

content.prompt:
A hemispherical bowl is carved out of a solid block of marble, as shown.

After the bowl is carved, the volume of marble remaining is $\left(6-\frac{18}{125}\pi\right)\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the radius of the hemisphere.

spec.description: Rectangular block with an elliptical circular opening and dashed hidden hemispherical cavity profile. The unknown cavity radius is not inferred from drawing proportions. Ordinary outlines and hidden geometry use black; hidden geometry remains dashed.
spec.mathematics: Block dimensions 2 m by 2 m by 1.5 m; hemispherical cavity of unknown radius.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source dimensions and centre marker are visible.

answer.short:
$r=0.6\text{ m}$.

Subtract the remaining marble volume from the block volume, then use half the sphere-volume formula.
answer.worked:
The block volume is
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{block}}&=2\times2\times1.5\\V_{\text{block}}&=6\text{ m}^3.\end{align*}$$
The removed hemisphere has volume
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{hemisphere}}&=6-\left(6-\frac{18\pi}{125}\right)\\V_{\text{hemisphere}}&=\frac{18\pi}{125}\text{ m}^3.\end{align*}$$
Using half the volume of a sphere,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3&=\frac{18\pi}{125}\\r^3&=\frac{18\pi}{125}\times\frac{3}{2\pi}\\r^3&=\frac{27}{125}\\r&=\sqrt[3]{\frac{27}{125}}\\r&=\frac35\text{ m}\\r&=0.6\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
